# Introduction

Two chapters across the modern conservation-genomics toolkit: (1) the new Global
Biodiversity Framework (GBF) genetic-diversity indicators on the endangered green
peafowl (*Pavo muticus*), and (2) realized-vs-masked genetic load in the inbred
Scandinavian wolf (*Canis lupus*). The cross-cutting thesis: **each verdict is
fragile to analyst choices** — filtering stringency, N_e method, and whether
population structure is modeled.

# Methods

## Data

- **Green peafowl** — Dong et al. 2021, Dryad `10.5061/dryad.ffbg79ctc`. 31 modern +
  6 museum genomes → 22 unrelated across 3 populations (Yunnan, Vietnam, Thailand).
- **Scandinavian wolf** — Smeds & Ellegren 2022, Dryad `10.5061/dryad.7m0cfxpzj`.
  WGS + VEP + GERP → turnkey genetic load.

## QC & filtering

Two callsets (structure/N_e vs diversity); thresholds in `config/config.yaml`; kin
screen before structure/N_e. *(Phase 1.)*

## Contemporary N_e and the fragility cube

The parameter sweep `{filter} × {method} × {structure}` → `results_cube.parquet`.
*(Phase 2.)*

## GBF indicators

N_e > 500 indicator; Populations Maintained; N_c proxy contrast. *(Phase 3.)*

## Genetic load & ROH (wolf)

Streaming VEP × GERP → realized vs masked; `bcftools roh` → F_ROH. *(Phase 4.)*

# Limitations

We claim *risk*, not demonstrated inbreeding depression. Small per-population n
yields wide CIs; ascertainment and (for low-coverage data) genotype-likelihood
caveats apply. The fragility cube quantifies, rather than hides, this uncertainty.

# Reproducibility statement

`conda env create -f environment.yml`; `renv::restore()`; `snakemake --use-conda`.
All thresholds in `config/config.yaml`; the full DAG re-runs from scratch.
